about: Editor spec §64, axioms_checker: graphs that keep every axiom, and graphs that break each one a single graph can break, with the problems the check must give. A case gives its graph as blocks the reader reads, or as things and links made by hand (graphs), for a break no block can write. packages/graph-spec/test/axioms.test.mjs and python/graph_spec/tests/test_axioms.py both answer them.

cases.name: a draft graph that keeps every axiom gives nothing
A1: a thing held under a name that is not its id

answer.law: Each thing has one id, and no other thing in its graph has it.
answer.message: thing 'a' is held under the name 'a' but its id is 'b'
answer.fix: keep each thing under its own id

cases.name: A2: a link with no thing at its far end, and A4 waits

answer.law: Every link starts and ends at a thing that is in the graph.
answer.message: link a-[:OWNS]->gone has no thing at its far end, 'gone'
answer.fix: write the thing it names, or take the link out

cases.name: A3: a kind and a link type the graph's own schema does not declare

answer.law: Every thing and every link has a type its schema declares.
answer.message: thing 'b' has the type Widget, which the schema does not declare
answer.fix: declare Widget in the schema, or use a type it declares

answer.law: Every thing and every link has a type its schema declares.
answer.message: link a-[:HOLDS]->b has the type HOLDS, which the schema does not declare
answer.fix: declare HOLDS in the schema, or use a type it declares

cases.name: A4: a list value the flat projection cannot write

answer.law: Reading is a function: the same text gives the same graph, and writing it out and reading it back changes nothing.
answer.message: graph g does not come back the same when it is written out and read again: the flat projection cannot write it
answer.fix: keep to values the flat projection can write, such as text, numbers, dates and true or false

cases.name: A7: a word not on the scale, and a range from high to low

answer.law: A likelihood is a word on the graph's scale, and a range never runs from high to low.
answer.message: thing 'c1' has the likelihood 'probable', which is not on the scale
answer.fix: use a word on the scale, with the lower word first

answer.law: A likelihood is a word on the graph's scale, and a range never runs from high to low.
answer.message: thing 'c2' has the likelihood range 'very-likely' to 'unlikely', which runs from high to low
answer.fix: use a word on the scale, with the lower word first

cases.name: A8: two successors, and a loop of supersession

answer.law: An item has at most one successor, and following successors never comes back to the start.
answer.fix: give each item one successor, and supersede only something older

answer.fix: give each item one successor, and supersede only something older
